pr.title: Level Time Tracker 2.0: a new look, for Midnight and WoW Forever
pr.body:
Rebuilds Level Time Tracker from scratch in the style of GuildLedger and HandyNotes Traveler. It's one addon for World of Warcraft: Midnight (12.1.5) and World of Warcraft: Forever (1.60.1). Merging this releases 2.0.0 to CurseForge, and the commit message becomes the changelog.

- Saved variables v2. Data is migrated from 1.x: old times are kept, levels 1.x couldn't time are marked "not timed", and broken values are dropped.

- Removes core.lua, which the TOC listed as Core.lua, and the unused Graph.lua.
- Midnight's secret values are unwrapped before use.

pr.title: Add projects dashboard with plain-English update feed
pr.body:
Adds a live dashboard of the public GitHub projects at https://gasteren.github.io/dashboard/, with a feed of updates explained in plain English by GitHub Copilot.
What's included
- Site (site/, plain HTML/CSS/JS): overview totals, "Latest updates" feed with a project filter and collapsible technical details, activity chart, language mix, and project cards (description, language, last update, latest release, commits, stars, GitHub/CurseForge/website links). Light and dark modes, mobile-friendly.
- Build (scripts/build.mjs): reads public data with the workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN (ETag caching, rate-limit guard), only for repositories that are explicitly private: false + visibility: public, and refuses to publish anything outside that set.
- Summaries: Copilot CLI (gpt-6-luna, falls back to gpt-5.6-luna) with tools denied, no MCP servers or custom instructions, prompt via stdin. Only new updates are sent, batched up to 15 per call, each summarized once; identical changes across projects share one summary and one card. Bot-only pushes (like the old irosec-homelab stats sync) are folded into a weekly "Automatic updates" card, skipped by the AI and left out of totals and the activity chart.
- Cost caps: --max-ai-credits 30 per call, 20 credits per run, 100 per 24 hours, 4 calls per run. A call whose usage can't be read counts as the full 30.

pr.title: v1.5.1: going back to the title screen or collection menu no longer gets stuck
pr.body:
Player report
"van game naar title screen loopt vasttt" (from the game to the title screen, it gets stuck). Endless loading screen, KH1, hotfix 1.5.0, PC-370E.
In the session log, WaitTitleProject.exe starts, KH1 exits with code 0x1, and the bootstrapper exits with 0. No game or Launcher starts after that, so the loading screen stays forever.
Cause
This was a hotfix bug, not a game bug. When axaAppMain returns, the game's startup code writes the exit code into the shared memory Mare_mem. The collection's bootstrapper (KINGDOM HEARTS HD 1.5+2.5 ReMIX.exe) reads it when the game ends to decide what comes next:
The Quit Game fix replaced the destructor call with TerminateProcess, which also skipped that write. As a result, both "back to title screen" and "back to the collection menu" ended on WaitTitleProject.exe's endless loading screen.
Fix
- Quit fix:
- Before TerminateProcess, the patch calls the game's own Mare_mem writer with the exit code. The writer is found by signature (identical in all five games) and must load the name "Mare_mem".
- TerminateProcess is now called through the game's import slot. The patch is 19 bytes (22 with the diagnostic marker), so it fits every game's region, including Re:CoM's 22 bytes.
- If the writer or the import can't be found, the fix is not used at all.
- Safety net: if WaitTitleProject.exe is the only KH program left for WaitScreenCloseSeconds (15 s), the wrapper closes it, tells the player to start the game again, and reports it. This c…

pr.title: Fix fishing filters not loading
pr.body:
The fishing filter hasn't loaded in-game since 540069b (2026-03-17). This fixes it and ships as 1.0.1.
Cause
In DF-db.lua, the hat entry added in 540069b has no trailing comma:
Lua reaches the next [255157] = true entry and fails to compile the whole file (DF-db.lua:187: '}' expected (to close '{' at line 24) near ''). WoW skips any file that doesn't compile, so addonTable.Dragonflight is never set and core.lua registers no filter. DF-db.lua has failed to compile at every commit from 540069b through main.
Changes
- DF-db.lua: adds the missing comma and corrects the item ID to 239638, [Elegant Artisan's Fishing Hat. The old ID 2396338 had an extra digit.
- AdiBags_fishing.toc: changes ## Version from 1.0.0 to 1.0.1. core.lua reads the version from the TOC, so no other file needed a change.
The ## Interface: lines, the CurseForge workflow, file encodings and line endings are unchanged.
Verification
- Compiled every file the TOC loads (expansion.lua, DF-db.lua, core.lua) with PUC Lua 5.1 (loadstring, the same check as luac -p) and with LuaJIT 2.1. All of them pass. Before the fix, DF-db.lua failed with the error above; I found no other syntax errors.
- Loaded the addon under Lua 5.1 the way the client does: in TOC order, on top of the real LibStub, CallbackHandler-1.0 and AceAddon-3.0 plus AdiBags' own core/EventHandlers.lua (ABEvent-1.0), core/Boot.lua and core/Filters.lua, with only client APIs mocked. The run fires ADDON_LOADED, then PLAYER_LOGIN, then PLAYER_ENTERING_WORLD.…

- No code reads the TOC Version field. There are no GetAddOnMetadata calls anywhere in the repo.

Merging into main triggers the CurseForge upload, and the head commit message becomes the CurseForge changelog. The commit message ends with a Co-authored-by trailer. If you squash-merge, you can delete that line in the merge dialog to keep it out of the changelog.

Resets the addon's own version so all WoW addons start aligned at 1.0.0.
Change
- HallOfFallenHeroes.toc: ## Version: 12.1.5 → ## Version: 1.0.0
That's the only change. Line endings and encoding are unchanged, so the diff is a single line.
Left untouched on purpose
- ## Interface: 120007, 120100, 120105
- game_versions: "12.1.5" in .github/workflows/curseforge-upload.yml. That's the WoW game patch, not the addon version.
- This repo has no bundled Libs/ TOCs.
Runtime version checks
None. HallOfFallenHeroes.lua never reads the addon version (no GetAddOnMetadata / C_AddOns calls or version comparisons). The HoFH_LastDeath saved variable is overwritten without any migration logic, so going from 12.1.5 down to 1.0.0 is safe.
Release note
Merging this into main starts the Upload to CurseForge workflow. The workflow uses the head commit message as the CurseForge changelog, so merge only when you're ready to release.

pr.title: Fetch addon stats and activity on the server, retire the GitHub sync
pr.body:
The addon stats came from a GitHub-hosted workflow:
- A cron job on dockerserver dispatched it every 10 minutes, and the workflow's own */30 schedule ran it too.
- Every run committed data/*.json to main (about 144 bot commits a day) and emailed on every failure, such as run 39783019815's CurseForge TLS reset.
This PR moves the fetching onto the server and retires that workflow.
What changes
- site/fetcher/: a small Python service (standard library only, python:3.13-alpine) next to the site in the same compose project. It fetches once at start, then just after every 10-minute mark (UTC), which is what the page's "next sync" countdown expects.
- CurseForge: slugs are resolved to project IDs once, then each cycle is a single POST /v1/mods request instead of 17 calls.
- Activity feed, without a GitHub token: one unauthenticated GET /users/Gasteren/repos per cycle. Commits are fetched only for repos whose pushed_at changed, so about 6-12 requests an hour against the 60/h limit. ETags wouldn't help here, because unauthenticated 304s still count.
- Failures: it retries with backoff on connection resets, TLS errors, 429 and 5xx. A failed cycle keeps the last good files, and writes are atomic.
- Health instead of emails: the container turns unhealthy, visible in Portainer, when the stats are older than 35 minutes or the activity feed older than 2 hours. Reasons show in docker logs and the healthcheck output.
- Hardening: it runs as uid 10001 with no capabilities and no-new-privilege…

pr.title: Version-control the wiki site, overhaul its design, and make addon stats live
pr.body:
The site behind wiki.irosec.com only existed on the Docker host, and addon download numbers only changed when gh-runner-irosec rebuilt the whole image for every stats commit. This PR fixes both and gives the site a visual overhaul with the same fonts and colors.
What changes
Site source in the repo (site/)
- The Astro Starlight site is imported as it runs in production (Astro 5.18.2, Starlight 0.30.6, including the 127.0.0.1 healthcheck fix). package-lock.json pins those versions and the image builds with npm ci.
- Content stays where it is edited today. site/scripts/sync-content.mjs copies the docs folders and data/*.json into the site before dev and build.
- docker-compose.yml and a whitelist .dockerignore at the repo root build from the repo root. .env never enters the build context.
- "Edit page" links pointed at a starlight-wiki/ folder that never existed. They now open the real files.
Live numbers without the runner
- nginx serves /api/addon-stats.json and /api/recent-activity.json from the same origin, proxied from raw.githubusercontent.com. DNS is resolved per request through Docker's resolver (so a DNS outage can't stop nginx from starting), TLS is verified, responses are cached for 60s, and the last good copy is served if GitHub is unreachable. The ref comes from LIVE_DATA_REF (default main).
- The page swaps in the live values, shows "synced Xm ago / next sync in mm:ss" following the 10-minute cron, and keeps the build-time values if a fetch fails. GitHub's raw CD…

pr.title: Fix the protected function error in the Options on WoW Forever
pr.body:
Fixes [ADDON_ACTION_FORBIDDEN] AddOn 'AfkDelight' tried to call the protected function 'IsUserOAuthed()' on WoW Forever.
Cause. AfkDelight's options were rows in Blizzard's shared Settings list (vertical layout). Two Settings API calls that ran inside AfkDelight's own code left its taint on data the Options search reads without securecallfunction: CreateSettingsButtonInitializer(..., addSearchTags = true) creates searchTags, read by MatchesSearchTags on every search, and SetParentInitializer sets parentInitializer, read in OnSearchTextChanged. When the search results included Social's Discord sign-in button, drawing it called the protected C_Discord.IsUserOAuthed() and the game blocked it. The reported stack trace (from SettingsPanelMixin:OnSearchTextChanged) matches Forever build 70707 line for line. Recycled list rows could carry the same taint: CallbackHandleContainerMixin:Unregister rewrites handles under the row's taint, and the Discord display-name dropdown (same template as AfkDelight's dropdowns) checks IsUserOAuthed() in its modify predicate.
Fix. AfkDelight registers its own canvas page (Settings.RegisterCanvasLayoutCategory) built only from its own frames, so it never touches Blizzard's shared rows:
- Same options, order, sections and greying of dependent options, with the measurements of Blizzard's settings lists.
- Background and character animation are radio buttons (no dropdown menus).
- Tooltips use GameTooltip; the Settings checkbox template's hover script,…

pr.title: Fix the low-level whisper filter letting low-level players through
pr.body:
In "Low-level only" mode, whispers from players at or below the level threshold were never blocked unless the sender was your target, mouseover, focus or in your group. For everyone else the level stayed unknown, so the whisper was held for 2 seconds and then shown anyway. With the threshold set to 3, level 1 players could still whisper you.
Changes (WhisperFilter.lua)
- Level lookup: reads the sender's level from the whisper's sender GUID (CHAT_MSG_WHISPER arg12). Retail and Forever return it as the 8th value of GetPlayerInfoByGUID (nilable), which is the approach BadBoy_Levels uses. The old unit-based lookup and 2-second wait remain as a fallback when no level is available, for example on Classic, and the GUID is passed through that path too.
- Whitelists: friend, Battle.net, guild and group checks use the GUID first (C_FriendList.IsFriend, C_BattleNet.GetGameAccountInfoByGUID, IsGuildMember, C_PartyInfo.IsGUIDInGroup) and fall back to the old name scans. This lets them match Forever's realm-less "First Last" names.
- GM/DEV whispers: whispers flagged GM or DEV are never filtered.
- Deferred whispers: each held whisper has its own timers. Before, a second quick whisper from the same sender replaced the first, and the first was lost.
- Secret values: guarded with issecretvalue (only when the function exists) before any comparison.
Block-all mode, BN whispers, cross-chat-frame dedup, the notice cooldown, login grace and the filter log behave as before.
